title: Brain Atrophy Analysis in Dementia
summary: A published computer-vision study that analyzes longitudinal MRI images to quantify structural brain changes associated with dementia.
landingDeck: Published at IEEE ICRITO 2022, the study applies image processing to longitudinal MRI scans to measure brain atrophy and examine structural change over time.
landingHighlights: Frames dementia analysis as measurement of longitudinal structural change in MRI data.
Uses Python and OpenCV image-processing steps to extract quantitative atrophy indicators.
Separates the publication record from the later four-class TensorFlow classification notebook.
problem: Dementia progression appears as structural change across MRI scans taken over time. The research question was how image processing could turn those scans into repeatable measurements of brain atrophy.
approach: The study applies a computer-vision pipeline to longitudinal MRI images, extracts structural measurements, and compares change across scans to characterize atrophy associated with dementia.
output: A peer-reviewed five-page paper published in the proceedings of the 2022 10th International Conference on Reliability, Infocom Technologies and Optimization (ICRITO), pages 1234–1238.

methodology.evaluation: The publication reports the image-processing workflow and its measurements on longitudinal MRI data. The paper is the source for its experimental details and findings.
methodology.boundary: Current evidence covers retrospective image analysis reported in the paper. Prospective diagnostic performance and patient-care use require separate clinical validation.

role: I co-authored the study and built the Python/OpenCV image-processing pipeline used to quantify structural change in the MRI scans.

pageSections.description: The study uses computer-vision methods to quantify atrophy visible across MRI images collected over time.
pageSections.context: Neerav Chaudhary and Sourabh Singh Verma published the paper at IEEE ICRITO in 2022.

pageSections.title: Turn visual change into a quantitative signal
pageSections.description: Longitudinal scans show how anatomy changes between imaging sessions.
pageSections.markdown:
The project examines brain atrophy as a measurable change across MRI scans. Its computer-vision pipeline prepares the images, isolates structural information, and derives measurements that can be compared over time.

The published analysis defines the research claims. A prospective diagnostic product would require a separate clinical study and patient-care validation.

pageSections.title: The publication and classification notebook are separate studies
pageSections.description: The paper covers longitudinal atrophy measurement. The later repository covers four-class image classification.
pageSections.markdown: The four-class TensorFlow notebook uses folder labels and CNN ensembles to predict dementia stage from images. It is documented on its own project page because its data pipeline, model task, and repository evidence differ from the published brain-atrophy study.
